subject: Kestrel Health — thundering-herd keepalive failures and exec escalation
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@kestrel.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T08:14:22-07:00
Subject: Intermittent drops / spike in 5xx+429 — seen after yesterday's traffic surge

Irene,

Quick heads-up from our side — after the marketing blast yesterday we saw a big spike in client retries that correlated with a sustained increase in 5xx and 429 responses from your streaming API. Symptoms: sessions silently drop (clients report idle disconnects), large numbers of duplicate requests from the front-end retry logic, and elevated p95/p99 latencies.

Impact: a subset of users saw partial transcripts and several transactions failed end-to-end. We started seeing the pattern around 07:30 PDT and it's intermittent but recurring. Attached a short p95 export and a trimmed connection trace.

Can we get an urgent triage? We're prepping an all-hands with our ops and need a concise status for our CTO.

Attachments: kestrel_p95_report_20270630.pdf, connection-trace-20270629.log

— Alex
Senior SRE, Kestrel Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T08:32:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops / spike in 5xx+429 — seen after yesterday's traffic surge

Alex — thanks for the report and the traces. We're pulling telemetry now and kicked off a quick analysis run. Initial ask: can you confirm whether clients are using aggressive retry windows (sub-500ms) and whether keepalive intervals were changed in your rollout? That pattern often amplifies transient 429s into a retry storm.

We'll prioritize a hotfix if we find a systemic issue. Karthik is looped in to lead the immediate investigation. I will send an internal exec note in the next hour once we have a short summary.

Irene Choi
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded attachment stubs ---
- kestrel_p95_report_20270630.pdf (11 pages)
- connection-trace-20270629.log (3.2MB, trimmed)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:05:47-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops / spike in 5xx+429 — seen after yesterday's traffic surge

Alex / team — I dug into the traces and service metrics. Summary:
- We see a correlated spike in TCP connection churn and upstream 503/502 errors in the inference frontends starting ~07:25 PDT.
- Keepalive probes are failing midway through synthesis for sessions that have long-running idle windows; idle TCP timeouts at the edge appear to be shorter than the client keepalive interval.
- Client retry timers in the Kestrel frontend are aggressive and do not incorporate exponential backoff for 429s — we observe repeated immediate reconnect attempts which look like a classic thundering-herd (retry amplification).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low-risk, ~15–30m roll):
1) Temporarily increase edge idle timeout to 120s (from 30s) to reduce premature disconnects.
2) Enable session pinning to worker nodes for in-flight conversations to avoid KV cache misses.
3) Push a transient 429-specific circuit breaker: degrade non-essential streaming to a shorter keepalive interval and return a controlled backoff hint header.

I'll open INF-8729 and attach a mitigation runbook. If you can confirm client retry behavior we can work with you to smooth the retry window in the next client release.

Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-runbook-v1.md

> On 2027-06-30 08:32, Irene Choi wrote:
> > Alex — thanks for the report and the traces. We're pulling telemetry now and kicked off a quick analysis run.
From: Alex Rivera <alex@kestrel.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@kestrel.ai
Date: 2027-06-30T10:12:01-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops / spike in 5xx+429 — seen after yesterday's traffic surge

Thanks Karthik — this matches what our SREs observed. Quick answers:
- Our client retry window was tightened for that release to retry every 400ms (we pushed a patch to reduce perceived latency).
- Keepalive intervals are 90s on our clients.

Impact numbers for the executive briefing: ~3.8% of active sessions saw at least one silent disconnect; ~0.9% of requests surfaced as duplicate retries; customer support tickets spiked ~14% for the affected cohort between 07:30–09:00 PDT.

We need two things from Redwood:
1) A short executive summary we can show our CTO in 30m (what happened, immediate mitigations, and when traffic will be stable).
2) A proposal on customer remediation (credits/discount) — procurement is cc'd.

Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T12:08:33-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent drops / spike in 5xx+429 — seen after yesterday's traffic surge

Irene / team — drafting an exec-facing note for leadership and Kestrel. Draft summary (for approval):
- Incident: transient increase in 5xx/429 and idle stream disconnects caused by combinatorial effect of aggressive client retry timers + short edge keepalive TTLs during a traffic surge.
- Impact: ~3.8% sessions affected; Kestrel supplied p95 report attached.
- Immediate action taken: increased edge idle timeout to 120s (active), enabled session pinning, applied 429 circuit-breaker with backoff hint.
- Next steps: coordinate a client-side patch to increase retry backoff and align keepalive intervals; run 48h monitored canary.
- Remediation proposal: offer Kestrel a one-month service credit on their monthly bill; procurement to confirm.

Approving this language and the credit proposal would let me send the official note and the DocuSign credit doc. Sean — any objections to the one-month credit?

Marissa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit_proposal_draft.docx
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex@kestrel.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T15:42:09-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops / spike in 5xx+429 — seen after yesterday's traffic surge

Team — final status update to close the loop for now:
- We implemented the three mitigations at 09:10 PDT; observed immediate reduction in connection churn and 5xx/429 rate returned to baseline by ~10:05 PDT.
- Kestrel SREs have patched client retry logic to add exponential backoff; we validated with a controlled load test at 14:00 PDT.
- INF-8729 created to track the full postmortem and longer-term fixes. JIRA: INF-8729.
- Marissa: please proceed with the one-month credit offer; Sean has approved offline. We'll send the DocuSign link once procurement confirms terms.

I'll keep the ticket open for the postmortem write-up and will add the end-to-end timeline and telemetry. Thanks everyone for the fast turn.

Irene Choi
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
